pr_title: fix: set strings as attributes, non-strings as properties if property exists
pr_body:
Alternative to #12734. Closes #12664. This feels like a more principled approach to the problem: if something is a non-string and exists as a property on the element, set it as a property, otherwise set it as an attribute.

This allows us to handle some of the platform's oddities gracefully, without needing to ship a lookup to the browser: if a component contains `<div translate="no">`, then we disable translation on that element (with `div.setAttribute('translate', 'no')`). If it contains `translate={false}`, we achieve the same outcome with `div.translate = false`.

~~Draft because I just realised that we still need a lookup for SSR~~

issue_context.title: Svelte 5: Some boolean attributes are incorrectly rendered with `<svelte:element>`.
issue_context.body: ### Describe the bug Related to https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/12643 and https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/12649. https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/12649/files#diff-87ec8cbb1aa898b9a6bc0e9dde2e355df357844becd562b80386d0bf4713b57fR344-R345 - there are other HTMLElement properties. Here's a possibly incomplete list: * [autofocus](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/autofocus) * [draggable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/draggable) * [hidden](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/hidden) * [inert](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/inert) * [isContentEditable](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/isContentEditable) (the related HTML attribute `contenteditable` has more values) * [spellcheck](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/spellcheck) * [translate](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/translate) Either way, new properties / attributes will be added over time. ### Reproduction [Reproduction link](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE5WPQWrEMAxFr2LUxWwCsw9JoOeou_DY8sTUkYOtFIrx3UuamHGHbooW0n8SgpfBOo8J-rcMpBaEHl7XFTrgr3UP6RM9I3SQwhb1ToYD9ehxQWLBs0tjlqAkFDFHtKOEFwnCRHW_q5vHUYJVPqEEoTYONugtNWx2xiA1wBFGbrIOxEiMxvHTu7Si93pG_dFAjoqSV7wfUpAwPVZXcaDh-tthkiRpuMWj_9sv__wvjV0lp1uNh1lNz16VN1YVPZxOMuXLOV3KnzZ7QQdLMM46NNBz3LC8l2-gFGPF8AEAAA==) ### Logs _No response_ ### System Info ```shell Svelte 5.0.0-next.202 ``` ### Severity annoyance
comments: Giving this the 5.0 milestone because it works in Svelte 4 - likely because since #11371 we get more properties (which fixes other bugs that Svelte 4 has), so we need to enhance that list we have

Some of those also are kinda different from `draggable`...`hidden` for example is a "boolean attribute": you can't set `hidden="false"`, it will still be hidden because the attribute is present. Same thing with `inert` even if it's correctly set as `false` it will still be inert. Same `autofocus`.

Also `contenteditable` seems to actually correctly reflect the value even in your screenshot.

We definitely want the change for `translate` and `spellcheck`

You're right, those are actually correct, and setting them to the string `false` is different to setting it to a boolean (or falsy) value.

I also don't quite understand the problem with `translate` and `spellcheck` - what is the problem with them? The look correct.

So in summary, all of those are actually fine?

> You're right, those are actually correct, and setting them to the string `false` is different to setting it to a boolean (or falsy) value.
> 
> I also don't quite understand the problem with `translate` and `spellcheck` - what is the problem with them? The look correct.
> 
> So in summary, all of those are actually fine?

`translate` and `spellcheck` have probably the same problem of `draggable`...they are setters on the element so if you try to do `element.spellcheck="string"` it treat that string as a truthy value and set spell check to "yes" even if the string was "no"...the fix is the adding those attributes to the list of attributes for which we always want to use `setAttribute`. All the rest seems fine to leave it like this imho.
